findings.detail: ASU Online's General Studies BA page describes: 'one core class led by faculty experts in the college, followed by three classes from each of FOUR topic areas, along with additional electives' (40 classes / 120 credits). The four topic areas are: (1) Global and natural science perspectives — think scientifically, interpret data, explore global challenges in science and technology; (2) Humanities, identities and society — culture, identity, human behavior via history, philosophy, arts; (3) National and civil service and professional studies — government, civic leadership, ethical practice in public/professional settings; (4) Organizations, technology and ethics — how organizations function, digital tools, applied ethics. NOTE: online wording is 'each of four' (all four required), not 'four of many'.
findings.source: cms.asuonline.asu.edu/online-degree-programs/undergraduate/general-studies; asuonline.asu.edu general-studies page

findings.detail: UCLA Extension is part of UCLA (WSCUC). Course numbering: XL 1-199 = equivalent to UCLA regular-session undergraduate courses, transferable for unit AND subject credit at all UC campuses (up to 36 units accepted by CSU); X 1-199 = undergraduate-level but not identical to UCLA courses, transferable for unit credit; XLC = concurrent enrollment in an actual UCLA daytime class ($497/unit undergraduate, Fall 2025); X 400-499 = post-baccalaureate professional courses — 'not undergraduate degree credit', require the home university's prior authorization. 1-99 lower division, 100-199 upper division. Most UCLA Extension Electrical & Computer Engineering offerings are X 400-level, so for the ASU degree only XL/X 1-199 courses (Physics XL 5A/5B/5C, Chemistry XL 14A/B, Math XL 31A/31B, CS/econ XL courses) are safe; XL 5A/5B are 5.0 units ($1,230-1,330 in 2026), Chem XL 14A and Math XL 31A $1,125 (2026). brief_for_planners: RULE SHEET — ASU BA in General Studies (plan code LSGNSBGS, College of Integrative Sciences and Arts, ASU Online), catalog years 2025-26 / 2026-27. Graduation: 120 credits minimum, at least 45 upper-division (ASU numbers 300-499; for transfer work the sending institution's level governs, evaluated course-by-course), ASU GPA 2.00, and a 30-credit ASU residency that the user has told us to ignore (note: the 42 ULC credits are posted on an official ASU transcript identically to campus courses, so they satisfy residency anyway). First-Year Composition: ENG 101 + ENG 102 (or ENG 105 alone; ENG 107/108 for non-native speakers) with C or better — 6 credits inside the Gold block. General Studies Gold (mandatory for catalog year 2024-25 onward), 35 credits: HUAD 6, SOBE 3, SCIT 8 (an approved 8-credit pairing with lab experience — in practice two 4-credit lecture+lab courses), QTRS 3, MATH 3, AMIT 3, CIVI 3, GCSI 3, SUST 3. Major block: ASU Online describes 'one core class led by college faculty' plus 'three classes from each of FOUR topic areas' (12 courses = 36 credits, at least 18 upper-division), plus electives to 120. The four official ASU Online topic areas are: (1) Global and natural science perspectives; (2) Humanities, identities and society; (3) National and civil service and professional studies; (4) Organizations, technology and ethics. The user's labels are NOT official names: map 'Technology & Government' onto areas 3 + 4 (POS 110/310, PAF 200, HST 306, OGL 200/300, CIS 105/308, PHI 306, TEM/CIS ethics-and-technology courses) and 'Socio-Technical Systems: Energy & Environment' onto area 1 (PHY 101/111, AST 111, BIO 100, GPH 111, SOS 100/110/111, SOS 3xx, PHY 194 Energy Matters) — but area 2 (humanities: PHI 101, REL 100, HST 327, ENG 301 types) must still receive 3 courses because the online wording is 'each of four', not 'four of many'. Course placement into areas beyond what CISA lists is an assumption to flag for the advisor. Core courses to substitute: ASU 101 The ASU Experience (1 credit; first-year orientation — resources, time management, academic integrity; usually not required of transfer students, so its substitute is essentially free: e.g., ULC TEL 111 or a first-term seminar); IDS 321 Interdisciplinary Issues (3 credits, upper-division rotating interdisciplinary-topics course — substitute with any upper-division interdisciplinary topics course from HES/UMPI/SNHU/BYU); IDS 402 Senior Seminar (formerly BIS 402; 3-credit upper-division interdisciplinary capstone; probably the 'one core class' — substitute with an upper-division capstone/senior seminar from another platform, ideally last on the timeline). After substitution, the freed 7 credits are refilled with elective volume; 150.334 − 120 = 30.334 credits of surplus already exist in the plan, so nothing is lost. ULC facts: $25 enroll + $400 to convert (=$425/course, 2026 price), C or better required, one year to convert, transcript-identical to campus courses (Gold codes attach automatically). Session-based ULC follow ASU sessions: Fall 2026 A/C start Aug 20, 2026 (C ends Dec 4), Fall B ≈ mid-Oct; Spring 2027 A/C start Jan 11, 2027, Spring B Mar 15, 2027; Summer sessions follow. Confirmed ULC inventory useful here: ENG 101, ENG 102 (8-wk session), SOS 100 (SUST), POS 110 (AMIT), HST 109/110 (AMIT), HST 101 (global), HST 102, GCU 102, PSY 101, COM 100, COM 225, ECN 211/212, CIS 105, CIS 194, CIS 308 (3 cr, 300-level, 8-week or on-demand — the only confirmed upper-division ULC), ACC 231, MAT 117/142/170, MAT 265 (16-week session), BIO 100 (4 cr lab, SCIT), AST 111 (4 cr lab science), CHM 114 (4 cr lab science), FSE 100 Intro to Engineering, PHY 194 Energy Matters (no lab), TEL 111, RAS 210 CAD/CAM (2026). NOT confirmed as ULC: PHY 111/121, EEE 120, MAT 266/267, CSE 205, STP 226, GPH 111, PHI 101, SOS 110/111 — do not plan them as ULC. A sensible 14-course ULC set: ENG 101, ENG 102, MAT 265 (MATH), CIS 105 or MAT 142 (QTRS), POS 110 (AMIT/CIVI), HST 101 or GCU 102 (GCSI), HST 102 (HUAD), SOS 100 (SUST), BIO 100 + AST 111 or CHM 114 (SCIT 8), ECN 211 or PSY 101 (SOBE), FSE 100, PHY 194, CIS 308 (upper-division). Transfer rules: ASU accepts C- or better from regionally accredited institutions; the 64-credit cap applies only to 2-year colleges (none of the six platforms); no other numeric cap on 4-year credit besides residency (ASU Online: up to 90); credit for CEUs/non-credit continuing education is refused, but UCLA Extension XL/X 1-199 and HES undergraduate-credit courses are degree-credit, not CEU; 'some ASU colleges may not accept nontraditional grading (pass/fail)' — take every course for a letter grade; quarter units convert at 2/3 (4 qu = 2.667; 32 qu = 21.33). Platform notes: SNHU (NECHE, $330/credit 2025-26 = $990 per course, 8-week terms, six starts/yr); Harvard Extension (NECHE, Harvard DCE transcript, letter grades at undergraduate-credit status, 4-credit courses, $2,260 per course for 2026-27 per an HES page — $2,160 in 2025-26; level assigned course-by-course by ASU); UMPI YourPace (NECHE, $1,800 flat per 8-week session, six sessions/yr, competency-based but final LETTER grades derived from rubric averages, so no pass/fail problem; 14 credits/session is aggressive but allowed); UCLA Extension (WSCUC via UCLA; use ONLY XL 1-199 or X 1-199 numbers — XL = identical to UCLA courses, subject+unit credit; X 1-199 = unit credit; X 400-499 are post-baccalaureate professional courses that are 'not undergraduate degree credit' and need prior home-university authorization — most ECE offerings are X 400s, so the 8 UCLA courses should be XL physics/chem/math/CS/econ, e.g., Physics XL 5A/5B/5C at 5 units ($1,230-1,330, 2026), Chem XL 14A / Math XL 31A ($1,125, 2026); 100-199 = upper-division); BYU Independent Study (NWCCU, BYU transcript, letter grades, $256/credit = $768 per 3-credit course effective Sep 3, 2025, 12-month window but completable in weeks). Practical cautions: (1) upper-division minimum 45 must be met mostly by SNHU/UMPI/HES/BYU/UCLA 100-199-level and ULC CIS 308 courses because nearly all ULC are 100-200 level; (2) 18 of the 36 topic-area credits must be upper-division; (3) SCIT must be an approved pairing — cleanest via two ULC 4-credit lab courses; (4) verify with CISA whether both IDS 321 and IDS 402 are required in 2026-27 (online page implies one core class) and whether ASU 101 is waived for transfers.

brief_for_planners:
Per-school shortlist, ranked by fit to Technology & Government / Energy & Environment / power electronics, with confirmed 2025-26/2026 prices. Assume all six schools transfer as regionally accredited credit; UCLA Extension X 4xx credit is the one transfer risk (ASU evaluates it case-by-case; X 1-199 would be safer but none relevant were found). Confidence flags: [C]=confirmed by snippet, [L]=likely, [A]=assumed.

ASU ULC (14 x 3 cr, $25 + $400 = $425 each, $5,950 total [C]). Strong subjects: engineering-track math and CS, economics. Ranked: MAT 265 Calc for Engineers I [C]; MAT 266 Calc II [L]; MAT 267 Calc III [L]; MAT 275 Differential Equations [L]; MAT 343 Applied Linear Algebra [L]; CSE 110 Principles of Programming [C]; CSE 205 OOP & Data Structures [L]; PHY 121 University Physics I + PHY 122 lab [A — not confirmed on ULC]; ECN 212 Micro [C]; ECN 211 Macro [C]; RAS 210 CAD/CAM [C]; CHM 113 [L]. Cheap filler: ENG 101/102 [L], COM 100 [L], PSY 101/SOC 101 [L], MAT 117/142/170 [L]. NOT on ULC: EEE 120, ASU 101, and (unconfirmed) POS 110/SOS 110/PAF 112 [A]. Prereq chain: MAT 170 → 265 → 266 → {267, 275, 343}; CSE 110 → 205; PHY 121 needs MAT 265 and co-req MAT 266. Caution: snippets show ULC session-based lengths of 12/16 weeks, not 7.5-week A/B; treat each ULC course as a semester-length (C-session) item unless the live calendar shows shorter sessions. FSE 100 is 2 credits — avoid or accept a 1-credit variance.

Harvard Extension (3 x 4 cr; $540/credit, $2,160 per course 2025-26 [C]; expect ~$2,200-2,300 in 2026-27). Strong subjects: physics with circuits, government, statistics, CS. Ranked: PHYS E-1bx Physics II: Electromagnetism, Circuits, Waves, Optics (Spring) [C] — the single best power-electronics foundation across all six schools; PHYS E-1ax Physics I (Fall) [C]; one GOVT course with technology/policy content — confirmed codes that recur: GOVT E-1820 Grand Strategy & US Foreign Policy, GOVT E-1897 American Foreign Policy, GOVT E-1113 Democratic Transitions [C]; ENVR E-101 Intro to Sustainability & Environmental Management [C — verify UG credit status]; STAT E-100 or STAT E-104 [C]; CSCI E-50 (CS50) [C]; CSCI E-7 Python, ECON E-10a, MATH E-15/E-21a/E-21b [L]. Labs (PHYS E-1axl/bxl) are separate small-credit courses [C], so a lecture-only registration keeps the clean 4 credits. Suggested trio: PHYS E-1bx + one GOVT (tech policy) + ENVR or STAT.

UCLA Extension (8 x 4 quarter units = 32 qu = 21.33 sem cr; ~$1,095-1,100 per course 2026 [C], ~$8,800 total). Strong subjects: sustainability, project management, data science. Ranked: ENVIRON X 400 Principles of Sustainability I [C]; MGMT X 401 Principles of Sustainability II [C]; ENVIRON X 402 Principles of Sustainability III [C]; two Sustainability Certificate electives (energy/climate ENVIRON X 4xx) [L]; MGMT X 444.1 Fundamentals of Project Management [C]; COM SCI X 450.00 Data Science Fundamentals [C] → COM SCI X 450.1 Introduction to Data Science [C]. No usable undergraduate power-electronics course exists (EC ENGR XLC 112 Intro to Power Systems is a restricted MS course) [C]; ECE offerings are mostly non-credit short courses. Quarters: Fall (late Sep), Winter (Jan), Spring (Apr), Summer (Jun), ~11 weeks each; two courses per quarter is comfortable.

BYU Independent Study (7 x 3 cr; $256/credit → $768 per 3-cr course, price effective 9/3/2025 [C]; $5,376 total). Strong subjects: introductory physics, calculus, statistics, government, economics. Ranked: PHSCS 106 General Physics 2 (E&M, circuits) [C]; PHSCS 105 General Physics 1 [C]; STAT 121 Principles of Statistics [C]; POLI 110 American Government & Politics [C]; ECON 110 Economic Principles [C]; GEOG 120 Geography & World Affairs / GEOG 130 Human Geography [L]; CS 142 Intro to Computer Programming [L]; ENGL 316 Technical Communication [L]; AHTG 100 American Heritage, HIST 201/202, PHIL 110 as filler [L]. MATH 112/113 Calculus are 4 credits each ($1,024) [C] — only use if the plan tolerates a 1-credit variance; MATH 213/215/290 not offered by IS [A]. Each course must be finished within ~15 weeks (self-paced, 12-month window).

UMPI YourPace (3 sessions x 14 cr = 42 cr; $1,800 flat per 8-week session, unlimited courses [C]; $5,400 total, cheapest per credit). Strong subjects: business/management, project management, general education. Authoritative list is catalog.umpi.edu 'YourPace Undergraduate Course Offerings' (catoid=10, navoid=475) — the codes below are reconstructed [A] and must be checked: POS 101 American Government; ENV 110 Intro Environmental Science; ECO 207/208 Economics; MAT 180 Statistics; COS 101 Computing; project-management/operations sequence (PMT/BUS 3xx); MIS data courses; BUS 210 Management, BUS 301 Business Law, BUS 385 HRM, BUS 420 Strategy; filler HTY 161/162, PHI 151, PSY 100, SOC 101, ENG 101/121, COM 200-level. Aim for 4-5 courses per session, weighting each session with two theme courses and two-three gen-ed/business fillers; YourPace's 300/400-level business courses also help the ASU upper-division minimum.

SNHU (4 x 3 cr; $354/credit 2026 → $1,062 per course [C], ~$4,248). Strong subjects: IT/programming, applied math, energy/environment gen-ed, interdisciplinary tech-and-society. Ranked: SCI-220 Energy and Society [C]; MAT-350 Applied Linear Algebra [C]; IT-140 Intro to Scripting (Python) [C] → IT-145 Application Development [C]; PHY-150 Intro Physics: Mechanics [C]; MAT-240 Applied Statistics [C]; IDS-403 Technology, Society and Culture [L] (best substitute for ASU IDS 402); ENV-101, POL-210, ECO-201/202, MAT-230 Discrete Math, DAT-220 [L]. 8-week terms, six starts per year.

Substitutions for ASU's required core [A, need advisor approval]: ASU 101 → SNHU SNHU-107 (1 cr) or a UMPI first-year seminar; IDS 321 → UCLA ENVIRON X 400 or HES ENVR E-101; IDS 402 → SNHU IDS-403. Freed ASU slots are refilled with ULC math/CS. Physics/circuits ladder across schools: BYU PHSCS 105/106 (algebra-based, cheapest) or HES PHYS E-1ax/E-1bx (best rigor) plus ULC PHY 121 if confirmed; math ladder entirely at ULC (265→266→267/275/343). Total tuition at the listed prices: ULC $5,950 + HES ~$6,480 + UCLA ~$8,800 + BYU $5,376 + UMPI $5,400 + SNHU ~$4,248 = ~$36,250 (2025-26/2026 prices).
